decoys.summary: The completed-recipe cache ignores dependency arguments. For `all: (emit 'alpha') (emit 'beta')`, it marks `emit` completed after the first invocation and skips the second, so the recipe never processes `beta`.
decoys.match_rule: A report must identify argument-insensitive recipe/dependency execution deduplication that skips a second invocation of the same recipe with different argument values.

refutation.evidence: Ran::mutex first indexes by the full recipe path and then by the complete Vec<Vec<String>> argument groups at src/ran.rs:14. The completion flag checked by run_recipe is therefore specific to that recipe-and-arguments pair. The probe ran `all: (emit 'alpha') (emit 'beta') (emit 'alpha')` and obtained exactly `alpha\nbeta\n` with exit 0: beta runs, while the repeated alpha is deduplicated. Direct CLI invocations with the same three argument sets also produced exactly those two lines. Two cases passed; see evidence/decoy-1.log and evidence/decoy-1/results.json.

decoys.summary: The quote() helper wraps its input in single quotes without escaping embedded apostrophes. Interpolating `quote("can't stop")` into a recipe command generates invalid POSIX shell syntax, so this ordinary value cannot be passed as one literal argument.
decoys.match_rule: A report must identify missing embedded-single-quote escaping in quote(), causing a POSIX shell parse failure or loss of the original single argument when the value contains an apostrophe.

refutation.evidence: quote() explicitly replaces every single quote with the POSIX shell sequence that ends the current single-quoted segment, emits a backslash-escaped apostrophe, and opens another single-quoted segment. It then surrounds the result with single quotes. A recipe running `printf '<%s>\n' {{quote(value)}}` printed exactly `<can't stop>\n`, proving that the apostrophe and space survive as one argument. Empty input and a value containing four apostrophes also passed, producing one output record each. Three cases passed; see evidence/decoy-2.log and evidence/decoy-2/results.json.

false_findings.title: Conditional expressions execute the unselected branch
false_findings.body: The conditional evaluator evaluates both branch expressions before selecting its result. For example, `x := if 'x' == 'x' { 'ok' } else { error('unselected') }` fails with the error from the else branch even though the condition is true. This breaks conditionals used to guard runtime failures or unavailable configuration values.

refutation.evidence: The Conditional match arm evaluates the condition and uses a Rust if/else to call evaluate_expression on exactly one branch. Both directions were tested: an error() in an unselected else branch yielded `ok-then`, and an error() in an unselected then branch yielded `ok-else`, both with exit 0. A separate selected error() returned exit 1 and the expected selected-error diagnostic, showing that the sentinel actually fails when reached. Three cases passed; see evidence/false-1.log and evidence/false-1/results.json.

false_findings.title: dotenv loading overwrites explicitly empty inherited variables
false_findings.body: With `set dotenv-load` and no `dotenv-override`, load_from_file treats an existing but empty environment variable as absent. If the caller sets `CONTROL_INHERITED=''` and .env contains `CONTROL_INHERITED=file-default`, both env('CONTROL_INHERITED') and recipe commands receive `file-default`. This defeats the caller's deliberate empty override and unexpectedly enables the file-provided configuration.

refutation.evidence: load_from_file inserts a dotenv key only when dotenv_override is true or env::var_os(&key).is_none(). An explicitly empty inherited value is Some(empty OsString), so it fails the insertion guard. The probe printed `env=<> shell=<>` for an inherited empty value and `env=<host> shell=<host>` for an inherited nonempty value. Enabling dotenv-override with the same .env then printed file-default in both positions, confirming that the fixture was loaded. Three cases passed; see evidence/false-2.log and evidence/false-2/results.json.

false_findings.title: Linewise positional arguments lose the first recipe argument to shell $0
false_findings.body: With `set positional-arguments`, run_linewise appends user arguments directly after the command passed to `sh -cu` without reserving an argument for shell $0. For `show +values:` invoked as `just show 'hello world' tail`, the shell consumes `hello world` as $0, leaving $# equal to 1 and only `tail` in $@. Recipes forwarding their arguments therefore silently drop the first value.

refutation.evidence: Before cmd.args(positional), run_linewise explicitly calls cmd.arg(self.name.lexeme()), placing the recipe name in shell $0. The public CLI probe with `show 'hello world' tail` printed `zero=<show> count=<2>`, followed by `arg=<hello world>` and `arg=<tail>`. Both values remain separate arguments and the first is present. One case passed; see evidence/false-3.log and evidence/false-3/results.json.

false_findings.title: Malformed replace_regex patterns panic instead of returning a function error
false_findings.body: replace_regex does not handle a failed regex compilation before attempting replacement. Evaluating `x := replace_regex('abc', '[', 'x')` unwraps the invalid-pattern result and panics, aborting just instead of returning its normal source-located function-call diagnostic. A typo in a justfile pattern therefore crashes the runner.

refutation.evidence: Regex::new(regex) is immediately followed by map_err(|err| err.to_string())?, so compilation failure returns Err before replace_all is reached. evaluate_builtin_function converts that Err into Error::FunctionCall with the source name token. The invalid '[' probe exited 1 with `Call to function `replace_regex` failed`, `unclosed character class`, and a justfile:1:6 source annotation, with no panic. A valid pattern returned `xbcx` with exit 0. Two cases passed; see evidence/false-4.log and evidence/false-4/results.json.

false_findings.title: Backtick capture trims significant trailing whitespace from command output
false_findings.body:
The command-output normalization used by backtick expressions strips all trailing whitespace instead of removing only the final line ending. For example, a backtick running `printf 'payload

'` yields `payload` rather than retaining one newline, and `printf 'payload  
'` loses the two spaces as well. This corrupts values whose trailing blank record or spaces are significant.

refutation.evidence: output_guard_stdout uses strip_suffix("\r\n").or_else(|| output.strip_suffix("\n")).unwrap_or(output): it removes at most one CRLF pair or one LF byte and does not trim spaces. Backticks call run_command, which calls this helper. Byte-exact CLI assertions confirmed that two terminal LFs leave one LF, two terminal CRLF pairs leave one CRLF pair, two spaces before a terminal LF remain, and trailing spaces without a newline remain. Four cases passed; see evidence/false-5.log and evidence/false-5/results.json.
